## Decision: do not merge

**Recommendation: keep both pages separate; link them instead.**

### What the actual pages contain

| | Post 100 | Post 200 |
|---|---|---|
| Title | Bicycle puncture repair | Tire size markings |
| Stored text | "We repair bicycle tire punctures and inspect tires at our workshop. Customers can bring the bike and describe when air loss occurs..." | "How to read the size markings on a bicycle tire. Different reader task from preparing for a puncture repair visit." |
| Reader task | Service intake — deciding to bring a bike in for repair | Reference — interpreting numbers printed on a tire sidewall |

### Why the shared phrase isn't a merge case
Both pages use the words "bicycle tire," but shared vocabulary is a *similarity signal*, not evidence of duplication. The decision record returned `stored_text_equal: false`, `seo_harm_established: false`, and `automatic_consolidation_eligible: false`. The two pages answer non-substitutable questions: a reader who wants to decode "700x25c" is not served by a workshop intake page, and a customer with a flat is not served by a sizing reference. Merging would force one page to serve two intents and would likely weaken both.

### What I did not do
No merge, no redirect, no noindex, no deletion, and nothing published. The linking recommendation is recorded as a plan only — it has not been applied to live content. If you want it implemented, I'd next propose specific in-body cross-links as draft edits for your approval.
